title: What a repository tells the harness about itself
description: `.agents/registry/project.json`: the paths the engine reads that belong to the project it serves, not to the engine. Every section is optional: a repository without one configures nothing there, and the reader says so. `Noetic.Harness.Project` reads it and checks what this schema cannot: that a context source's `same_as` names a declared source, that every source has a kind with its fields, and that the kb paths lie inside the repository.

name.description: The project's name, as the generated GEMINI.md heads itself.

adr.description: Where the decision records are, and how a number is written in a file name: `noetic-harness assign --adr N` refuses a number whose file exists (`<dir>/<prefix><N padded to digits>-`).

source_roots.description: The top-level directories a source path recorded at another checkout's absolute path is cut back to, so that it resolves here.

kb.description: The knowledge base's files: the extraction the index is built from, the glossary the context names terms from, the reading maps a profile reads first, the corpus sources resolve against.

services.description: What SessionStart probes on localhost, and the command it names when one does not answer.

tooling.description: The command telemetry names for a gate that could not run because its tool is missing.

beads.description: The guide SessionStart names when bd would use a second bead database.
`bd`, the work graph: SessionStart's ready list, the `beads` context source, `route --bead`, `prompt --task`, telemetry's `--file`, and the bead side of `assign`.

knowledge_base.description: Probing the knowledge store (Postgres) and Qdrant beside a `kb` answer. The answer is the files' either way.

jido.description: The `jido` dispatch adapter, whose module lives in `acme_agents`.

workers.description: The coordinator and cloud-worker protocol: `assign`, coordination records, profiles.

integrations.description: What the harness may reach outside itself. A switch that is absent is off: a repository has an integration only when it says so. Off is said by whatever needs it, never a failure of it; `route`, `context`, `gates`, `run` and `conduct` need none.

apps.description: The directory each app is a directory of: an app's files are `<apps>/<app>/…`.

test_suffix.description: How a test file's name ends; its extension is a test file's.

test_command.description: The command that runs test files, run in the app's directory, with the files appended.

build.description: The build directory, whose `test/lib` holds the compiled dependencies a fresh worktree is seeded with.

layout.description: Where an app's source and tests are, and how its tests run: what `noetic-harness environments` derives an environment from and verifies it with, and what a worktree is seeded with. A repository without it can neither derive nor verify an environment, and says so.

context.description: Context sources by key, the keys `capabilities.json` names under `context`. A key with no source here and no resolver in `Noetic.Harness.Context` is reported as not attached. `docs` ranks a glob's documents by the task's terms; `files` shows the named files that exist; `glob` lists what the globs match; `same_as` answers as another key does.
